response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT r.name AS name, SUM(res.points) AS tp FROM results res JOIN races r ON r.raceId = res.raceId GROUP BY r.name), a AS (SELECT AVG(tp) AS avgtp FROM t), k AS (SELECT t.name AS name, t.tp AS tp FROM t, a WHERE t.tp > a.avgtp) SELECT (SELECT SUM(tp) FROM k) AS total_points_sum, (SELECT AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) FROM results res JOIN races r ON r.raceId = res.raceId WHERE r.name IN (SELECT name FROM k) AND res.laps IS NOT NULL) AS avg_laps_all_results, (SELECT AVG(k.tp - a.avgtp) FROM k, a) AS avg_excess_over_average_total

assumptions.assumption: Race names are grouped by races.name, so the same Grand Prix across different years counts as one group. Results with no matching race are dropped by the inner join.
The average total is the simple average of the per-name totals, not weighted by the number of results. Totals are sums of results.points.
laps is stored as text and is cast to a number. Results with NULL laps are excluded from the laps average. Any non-numeric placeholder strings would cast to 0 and would need to be excluded too.
